flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
There was this time when I was working as a behavior technician where I would have to take away the iPad since they were really into the iPad, I would have to take it away and run programs with them. And there was a time where he really, really didn't want to. And I kind of had to redirect him with another program kind of like, oh, first we can do this and then you can get your iPad back. But he really didn't want to. And he started like throwing things, crying. So I would have to, and then I went back to him and I asked what was wrong. And he just said that he was very tired of working and tired of running programs. So we took a 10 minute break and he was very good after. He just was very like, like emotionally. Just tired of everything.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Can you share something you’ve learned about children or yourself over time that changed how you approach your work?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q9 Attempt 1]
When I was with my autistic brother, I really, really wanted to join a school or work in that career, working as a behavior technician. It helped me grow as a person and learn more about my brother and why he would do the things he would do or why he would act the way he was acting. And it made me learn more to take care of him and more to understand how he was feeling. So it made me grow as a person for my brother and then for the kids that I would work with. I loved learning how everyone was different and they weren't really the same. I left because the hours weren't as good as I wanted them to be. I would get two hours every other day and I kind of wanted a full-time position.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about how you physically care for infants or toddlers during routines like feeding, diapering, or comforting.
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q10 Attempt 1]
I have seven nephews, all boys, so I grew up teaching my, not teaching, sorry, learning how to do, not do diapers, change diapers, sorry, change diapers, feed babies every morning, bathe them at night, and it was an everyday routine with my nephews. So, that made me learn a lot on how to do things in a way to make it easier for myself. So, with diapering, I would always like to, since it was nephews, I would like to cover the top part with the diaper that was, that I'm using as, you know, and then wipe and clean, and then I'll close the diaper up, which was way easier than getting peed on or anything like that. And then, yeah. That's it. I would put, since, you know how babies get rashes sometimes, whatever my sisters had, like the ointments they had, I would just put it, and that was it for the diapering part.
